deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics. It is a bibliographical list, headed 'Academische Schriften', of Leonhard Euler's academy publications. The next page continues with Euler's pieces in the Miscellanea Berolinensia, the Berlin Mémoires, the Acta Eruditorum and the Miscellanea Taurinensia, and mentions 'lettres de Euler a Bernoulli', which settles the subject. The previous page is a printed German introduction to mathematics; the margin of this sheet repeats the same list.

Part 1, St Petersburg, with tallies of papers:
- Commentarii Academiae Scientiarum Petropolitanae, vols. II–XIV: 74.
- Novi Commentarii: 179.
- Acta (the word 'Novis' is struck out), up to Tom. IV pars II for the year 1780: 66.
- Sum: 74 + 179 + 66 = 319. The only computation on the page is this addition, and it is correct.
- Striking out 'Novis' is a correct self-correction. The 'Acta Academiae Scientiarum Imperialis Petropolitanae' ran for 1777–1782 and were organised by year and part. The 'Nova Acta' began only afterwards.

Part 2, Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences, Paris:
- 1765: 'Précis d'une théorie générale de la dioptrique'.
- 1778: 'Essai d'une théorie de la résistance qu'éprouve la proue d'un vaisseau dans son mouvement'.

Part 3, Recueil des pièces qui ont remporté les prix de l'Académie, by Recueil volume:
- Vol. 2: masting problem, 'Meditationes super problemate nautico de implantatione malorum' (1727 accessit).
- Vol. 4: 'Dissertatio de igne' (1738 prize); 'Inquisitio physica in causam fluxus et refluxus maris' (1740 prize, tides).
- Vol. 5: magnetic inclination and 'Dissertatio de magnete' (1743/1744).
- Vol. 7: inequalities of Saturn and Jupiter (1748 prize) and a related Jupiter piece.
- Vol. 8: 'De promotione navium sine vi venti' (1753); 'Investigatio perturbationum…' (1752 prize); 'Examen des efforts…' on roll and pitch (1759).
- Vol. 9: lunar theory and the secular equation (1770 prize); 'Nouvelles recherches sur le vrai mouvement de la lune' (1772).

Purpose: this appears to be a reading or acquisition list of Euler's works, most likely compiled by the young Gauss in the 1790s.
errors: No mathematical errors. The sum 74 + 179 + 66 = 319 is correct.
'que prouve' (as transcribed) should read 'qu'éprouve'. This is a slip in either the hand or the transcription.
'Recherches sur les irregularites de Jupiter' is probably an abbreviated or garbled title for a companion piece on the Jupiter–Saturn inequalities. This is unsure.

results.what: Catalogue of Euler's papers in the Petersburg Commentarii, Novi Commentarii and Acta (up to 1780), with counts 74/179/66 = 319, plus his Paris Mémoires and prize pieces
results.usually_credited_to: Euler bibliographies: N. Fuss's list (1783/1786); G. Eneström (1910–13)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bibliographic list of Euler's academy works with a trivial addition. That Gauss studied Euler intensively is well known. A personal Euler checklist is mildly interesting as evidence of his reading, but it contains no mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The tally of Euler's Petersburg papers is summed correctly.

transcription_corrections: 'Lc.' in the hand is 'Sc.' (Scientiarum), as the transcription already reads.
'v. II–XIV' may be written as 'u.' or 'v.' in the hand; the meaning is volumes II–XIV.

In 'Investigatio perturbationum' the hand writes something like 'Investigatio'/'Investigatis'; the correct title is 'Investigatio perturbationum quibus planetarum motus ob actionem eorum mutuam afficiuntur'.
